verified_facts: The USGS Great Basin release describes background conductive heat-flow maps made with weighted local regression that de-emphasizes measurements interpreted as locally convective outliers.

The release says its point coverage includes a heat-flow residual, interpreted as departure from estimated background conditions and potentially useful for identifying hydrothermal or groundwater influence.
The ScienceBase record publicly lists a 124.12 MB ZIP attachment named heat_flow_maps_and_supporting_data_for_the_Great_Basin_USA.zip.
sources.access_check: The official record and attachment listing were reachable. The archive was not downloaded, inspected, hashed, or co-registered in this review.
not_verified: Exact point-field schema, measurement-quality fields, license terms for redistribution, coordinate reference, and coverage within the competition footprint.
Whether the residual feature adds signal beyond the existing mirrored geothermal observations.

verified_facts: The USGS/DOE GeoDAWN record describes airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys over northern and western Nevada and eastern California, with variable survey specifications, terrain clearance, and aircraft/platform blocks.
The record states that line data, tie-line information, flight paths, and gridded products are included.
ScienceBase publicly lists CSV, geodatabase, grid, and GeoTIFF archive attachments, including some very large raw-line ZIPs.
sources.access_check: The public release page and attachment inventory were reachable. No raw archive was downloaded; exact competition-footprint intersection and product-level provenance remain unchecked.
not_verified: Per-line schema, processing fields needed for a cross-over analysis, local AOI coverage, and compatibility with the competition feature grid.

verified_facts: The repository record identifies the INGENIOUS Great Basin compilation and states CC BY 4.0 terms with attribution.
The record describes 2 m temperature probes, paleogeothermal sinter/tufa, wells and springs, aqueous geochemistry, heat flow, geodetic shear/dilation, slip/dilation tendency, and other data families.

Repository inspection confirms that active THCS/FCHD code already implements 2 m probes, paleogeothermal sinter/tufa, well/spring temperatures, silica/cation geothermometry, and volcanic-vent proximity. These data families alone are not new hypotheses.
sources.access_check: The official page was reachable and lists data products. No new archive was downloaded or schema-inspected in this review.
limitations: Exact AOI coverage and exact fields available for a separate hydrochemical-mixing analysis were not checked.
GDR terms require attribution; check the full license record for any product-specific conditions before redistribution.

verified_facts: USGS FDSN documentation supports rectangular latitude/longitude constraints and a producttype filter; focal-mechanism and moment-tensor products are listed examples.
The API also documents a count method, which can screen coverage before downloading event products.
sources.access_check: The official API documentation was reachable. A regional focal-mechanism query was attempted through the page-retrieval tool but failed to return; the AOI event count and product completeness remain unverified.
limitations: No event data were downloaded; the presence of an API endpoint does not establish useful local mechanism coverage.
